price_per_million.source: copied from reasoning_models_v1 (confirmed 2026-11-11); thinking tokens billed as output

research_concepts: shaper role (connector/organizer role) portability after a team change
cut share vs drive share in the pre-move play-type mix
role carryover with regression to the mean and menu-similarity confounds
methodological_questions: How is 'role travels' defined and measured (e.g. a post-move change in an organizational-function signature, Delta, against decoys)?
Is n=24 movers enough to detect a cut-minus-drive difference when the earlier effect was rho of about 0.27?
How are shapers and cut/drive shares derived from play-by-play and play-type records without outcome-derived labels?
How are menu-similarity, teammate/coaching change, and selection into moves controlled?
Can a pre-registered replication on movers not used in the earlier analysis be built from the 2025-26 data?

historical_evidence.finding: Among 92 connector movers, pre-move cut share predicted portability: rho=+0.265 (p=0.011, AUC 0.653); drive share rho=-0.278 (p=0.007); top cut tercile 65% portable (median Delta +0.167) vs bottom 35% (median -0.039); LOO AUC 0.622; permutation p=0.005; rho=+0.244 (p=0.020) after dropping Gafford. Notes: exploratory scripts, treated as a boundary condition, almost all other pre-move predictors null, same-pipeline validation only, limited by small sample.

Portability pairing variants: a KW p=0.047 (n=92) role-class stratification and an organizer-connector gap (MW p=0.07; bootstrap CI [-0.001,+0.180]) were reported; the organizer-connector CI includes 0 after correcting a menu-similarity confound. Limited by confounding and small sample.

Portability feasibility gate passed: 296 movers in prereg vs 294 in final output, with decoys available and displacement signature not collinear with play-type profile (rho 0.048 then 0.007). The mover count changed between prereg and final output.
Connector absence displaces team offensive identity more than usage-matched role absence (n=96 matched pairs); flagged for mechanical floor and small sample.
Play-type memory (including DRIVE lifts) was flat across lags and collapsed under within-team baselines; a team-quality confound.
Global play-type lag lifts disappeared after team-season demeaning.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Role-class (organizer vs connector) portability gaps without control for menu similarity
failed_approaches.why: The gap's CI includes 0 after the menu-similarity confound was corrected; the KW p=0.047 is population-level only (confounding, small sample).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Pooled play-type effects without within-team baselines
failed_approaches.why: The effect was a team-quality artifact (confounding).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Global lag curves of play-type effects
failed_approaches.why: The effect vanished after team-season demeaning.

evidence_establishes: A prior exploratory analysis on 92 connector movers found a positive association between cut share and portability and a negative one for drive share (FAM:SF-CHT-057, recorded as supported).
The project has a working portability pipeline with decoy-based Delta and a passed feasibility gate (FAM:SF-PAP-016).
Unadjusted play-type comparisons in this project have repeatedly been artifacts of team quality or menu similarity (FAM:SF-CHT-029, FAM:SF-APPS-073, FAM:SF-CHT-087).
evidence_does_not_establish: That the cut effect holds out of sample: FAM:SF-CHT-057 is exploratory, was validated only with the same pipeline, and has no recorded failure evidence.
That the effect is free of menu-similarity or team-context confounding; FAM:SF-CHT-087 found such a confound in a neighbouring comparison.
That the n=24 unit set in this task matches the 92-mover sample or the 'shaper' definition; no retrieved record defines 'shaper' or the unit set.
That the effect is a robust cut-vs-drive difference rather than a position or big-man effect (Gafford was influential; position splits were run, but the results are not recorded).
own_inferences: The question is probably a narrower, possibly holdout, version of FAM:SF-CHT-057: 24 movers may be the post-hoc subset or the new movers.
With n=24 and a true rho of about 0.27, power is only about 0.2 to 0.3, so a null would be uninformative and a significant result would likely overstate the effect (winner's curse).
If the 24 units were chosen after seeing the earlier result, the test is not confirmatory.
'Travel better' needs a single pre-specified binary or continuous portability measure, or the test is open to many analytic choices.
uncertainties: The definition of 'shaper' and of 'cut-heavy' or 'drive-heavy' (cut share vs cut minus drive; thresholds) is not given.
The origin of the 24 units is unknown (new 2025-26 movers, a filtered subset, or role-defined shapers).
Whether the 2025-26 data contain enough new movers with at least 3 decoys is unknown.
The outcome-label dependence of Delta and the amount of regression to the mean are unknown.
The mover counts in FAM:SF-PAP-016 changed between prereg and final output.

historical_effect.explanation: Without the history this would look like a small-n question to drop. FAM:SF-CHT-057 shows a prior supported but exploratory effect in 92 movers, and this makes a confirmatory replication on new movers worthwhile. FAM:SF-CHT-087, FAM:SF-CHT-029 and FAM:SF-APPS-073 push the design toward within-team and menu-similarity controls, and FAM:SF-CHT-057's exploratory status, rather than the n=24 sample, gives the case for a replication.

blocking_constraints.text: n=24 gives roughly 20-30% power for rho of about 0.27; about 100 movers would be needed for 80% power, so a standalone test of the 24 is not decisive.
Menu similarity, destination team context, and position (big men) must be controlled; FAM:SF-CHT-087 showed an apparent gap shrinking after such a correction.

prior_work.summary: FAM:SF-CHT-057 reported (exploratory, n=92 connector movers) that cut share predicts portability and drive share predicts the opposite. It was not confirmed on independent movers and no confounder-adjusted version is recorded. The retrieved records do not show that 'shapers' are the same units.

risks.text: n=24 is underpowered for the expected effect; a null is uninformative and a hit is inflated.
Menu similarity, destination team quality, coaching/teammate change and position can mimic a cut-vs-drive difference.
Movers are not random, and extreme pre-move signature values regress toward the mean after the move, which can look like non-portability.
'Portable' is defined from post-move Delta, and the role label and the cut/drive shares come from the same play-type records, so the two can be mechanically linked.
Many cut/drive operationalisations, terciles and position splits were explored previously; the forking paths are large.
Cut and drive shares and Delta are noisy for low-volume movers.
Pre-move features must use only pre-move games, and the moving window has to be fixed in advance.
Few possessions per mover on either side of a move and few decoys per mover.

design.estimand: Spearman rho between pre-move cut share minus drive share and post-move portability Delta (as defined in FAM:SF-CHT-057) among shaper/connector movers, adjusted for menu similarity and position. The contrast is cut-heavy vs drive-heavy tercile or half; the hypothesis is rho greater than 0.
design.unit: Player who changed team between seasons, one move per player, with a pre-move and a post-move window.
design.sample: Fix the 'shaper' definition before looking at the outcome. The confirmatory sample is movers not in the 92 of FAM:SF-CHT-057, chiefly 2025-26 movers; if the 24 are those, test them as a holdout. Otherwise pool the new movers with the old 92 and state this was done. Apply minimum pre-move and post-move possession thresholds and at least 3 decoys, as in FAM:SF-PAP-016.
design.power: At n=24 and rho=0.27, power is about 0.2-0.3, so report the confidence interval as the primary result and do not read a null as rejection. Aim for at least 100 movers for 80% power; if fewer, declare the study estimation-only.
design.controls: Menu-similarity between old and new team, destination team quality and coach change, pre-move usage, position/big-man indicator, minutes, within-team baselines (team-season demeaning), and an RTM-aware model that regresses Delta on the pre-move level of the same signature.
design.falsification: Permutation of cut/drive labels across movers (5000 shuffles); a placebo using non-movers' season-to-season Delta; and a check that the effect survives dropping the top influential players and the menu-similarity correction. The hypothesis is not supported if the adjusted rho CI includes 0 or the sign reverses.
design.multiplicity: One primary test (cut minus drive share vs Delta). Cut share alone, drive share alone, tercile hit rates and position splits are secondary and Holm-corrected.
design.decision_rule: Supported if the adjusted rho is positive with a one-sided 95% CI excluding 0 and the permutation p is below 0.05; rejected only if n is at least 100 and the upper 95% bound is below 0.15; otherwise report as inconclusive.
design.data_version: NBA per-game files and the play-type possession graph for 2022-23 to 2025-26 as of the 2026-08-08 data cut; 2025-26 regular season and playoffs complete. Freeze the mover list and thresholds before the post-move outcome is computed, and record any mover-count changes between prereg and final output.

methodological_questions: How is role portability defined and measured when a player changes team or context?
Is n=24 units enough to detect a difference in role stability between cut-heavy and drive-heavy shapers?
How are shaper roles and cut/drive composition derived from play-by-play and play-type records without outcome-derived labels?
How do regression to the mean, selection into moves, and teammate or coaching changes confound role carryover?
Can role classification be validated with reliable measures given sparse exposure per player?
args.query: Do cut-heavy shapers retain their structural role when moving between teams or contexts better than drive-heavy shapers? Prior studies of role portability, role stability, shaper classification, and cut versus drive action profiles.

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- search_documents(query): rank further study-family documents by text relevance; returns up to 10 families not yet returned.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-08-08, in the area of structural roles and influence):
Cut-heavy shapers' roles travel better than drive-heavy ones.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=24

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

Stage 1. Reply only with the retrieval call: {"action": "tool", "tool": "retrieve_history", "args": {"research_concepts": ["..."], "methodological_questions": ["..."], "query": "..."}}
